chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who chews the gum (of the tamarisk tree), so he said, 'Yes, if he wishes.'
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon.
ai.seo_question: Is chewing gum permissible while fasting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that chewing 'alk' does not invalidate the fast, as it is not considered food or drink in the strict legal sense. However, Shaykh al-Tusi notes that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan deemed this report 'not acted upon' (ghayr ma'mul bihi), likely due to the principle of caution (ihtiyat) or conflicting evidence in other narrations, illustrating the nuance between theoretical permissibility and practical legal application in Shia jurisprudence. This reflects the broader Shia methodology of weighing individual reports against established legal principles.
